title: TRIMRANGE accepts 3 arguments (0 none, 1 leading, 2 trailing, 3 both default), rejects fractional modes with #VALUE!, and returns #REF! on an all-blank input
statement: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527 on 26 catalogue calls (sheet dch9u_functions), TRIMRANGE(range, [trim_rows], [trim_cols]) takes at most three arguments and defaults both trim_rows and trim_cols to 3 (both margins). Code 0 keeps all margins, 1 trims leading blanks, 2 trims trailing blanks, and 3 trims both; string "2" coerces to 2 and TRUE coerces to 1, while non-integer 2.9, out-of-range 4 or -1, and a multi-area union (A1:A3,A5:A9) return #VALUE!. A completely blank range or array returns #REF! (not #CALC!). TRIMRANGE also accepts array constants (ROWS(TRIMRANGE({1,2},1)) is 1) and scalar numbers, text, or logicals. The trim-reference operators save in files as _xlfn._TRO_TRAILING(ref) for A1:.B9 (mode 2), _xlfn._TRO_LEADING(ref) for A1.:B9 (mode 1), and _xlfn._TRO_ALL(ref) for A1.:.B9 (mode 3), and evaluate identically to TRIMRANGE with both trim modes equal.
basis: 26 recorded Excel 16.0.20527.20088 readings in catalogue sheet dch9u_functions (rows 17-38 for TRIMRANGE and rows 39-44 for trim-reference operators) with Data!A1:A3 holding numbers, Data!A4:A20 blank, and Data!F1:F20 blank.
